title: Pictograms / Expressive strokes — Dark background

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Dark background

slide_intent: Separate the readable core from expressive color, because decorative depth should reinforce rather than obscure the symbol.
strategic_value: White productive strokes combined with controlled gradients can make IBM’s expressive pictograms distinct on black.
demonstration: Four pictograms on black combine white lines and circular points with broader colored gradient strokes; examples include a currency mark, connected circles, offset squares and nested curves.
practical_value: Use the dark-background expressive artwork rather than recoloring a light-background pictogram.

content_islands.name: Background selector
content_islands.spec: Show Dark background selected above the specimen.

content_islands.name: Expressive quartet
content_islands.spec: Align four contrasting pictograms horizontally on the black field, retaining white productive strokes and colored gradient strokes.

ingredient.name: Dark expressive pictogram layers
ingredient.role: Keep essential details legible while giving the symbol stronger visual presence.
ingredient.application: Use White productive strokes with the supplied dark-mode gradient artwork; keep the gradient layer fixed at 45° and masked by the expressive strokes.
ingredient.scope: IBM expressive pictograms. Do not change productive-stroke color or the supplied gradient’s angle and scale.

reference_purposes.Expression: White detail and luminous gradient paths demonstrate the expressive pictogram style on black.
reference_purposes.Application: The specimen shows the dark-background rendering of expressive pictograms.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying guidance requires White productive strokes on dark backgrounds, a stationary 45° gradient layer and approved two-color families; it prohibits altering the gradient angle or scale.
